posts.title: CHIEF VINCENT NEMIEBOKA MEETS AMANYANABO AND COUNCIL OF BOLO SE OVER UPCOMING DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS
posts.body:
The Executive Chairman of Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area, Chief Vincent Nemieboka DSSRS JP, today met with the Amanyanabo and Council of Bolo Se to brief them on the commencement of several development projects in Bolo Town.
‎
‎The meeting was convened on behalf of Alabo Boma Iyaye DSSRS, Executive Director, Finance and Administration (EDFA), Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), as part of ongoing efforts to facilitate development and improve infrastructure in the community.
‎

‎During the meeting, the Chairman informed the traditional institution of the planned commencement of the following projects:
‎
‎1. Renovation of Bolo Health Centre: The Rivers State Primary Health Care Board will undertake the renovation of the health facility to improve healthcare delivery in the community.
‎
‎2. Renovation of Bolo-Kira Link Road: The Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) will undertake the renovation of sections of the Bolo-Kira link road, which spans over two kilometres, to improve connectivity and ease the movement of people and goods. Inspection and evaluation has already started. 
‎
‎3. The Ogu/Bolo Local Government Council will commence the renovation of the Amanyanabo’s Palace. The building within the palace of the Amanyanabo of Bolo will be renovated to improve the condition of the traditional institution’s facilities.
‎[photo 2]
‎4. Construction of Internal Roads: The Ogu/Bolo Local Government Council will commence the construction of selected internal roads in Bolo Town to enhance accessibility within the community.
‎
‎In his remarks, the Amanyanabo of Bolo Kingdom, HRH Micha Acheseinimie Frank JP KSC, Bolo Luka VIII, expressed gratitude to Alabo Boma Iyaye and Chief Vincent Nemieboka for their interventions and commitment to the development of Bolo Kingdom.
‎
‎He particularly appreciated their efforts towards improving road infrastructure, facilitating the smooth movement of people and goods, and promoting the overall development of the community.
‎
‎The meeting reaffirmed the importance of collaboration between government institutions, development agencies and traditional leadership in advancing infrastructure development and improving the welfare of the people of Bolo.
‎
‎Media and Communications Unit
‎Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area

posts.title: Fifika Chiri Foundation Holds Two-Day Free Medical Outreach for Elderly Persons in Bolo Community
posts.body:
Ogu/Bolo LGA, Rivers State

The Fifika Chiri Foundation will hold its Annual Medical Outreach for elderly residents of Bolo Community on Thursday 12th and Friday 13th November 2026. The outreach is free and open to everyone aged 70 and above.

It will run daily from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. at the Bolo Civic Hall, Bolo Town, Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area.
Free Tests, Consultation and Medication
Beneficiaries will receive free medical services, including:

Eye test
Malaria test
Blood sugar test
HIV screening
Tuberculosis (TB) test (GeneXpert)
Urinalysis
Hepatitis screening
General medical check-up
Medical consultation
Provision of drugs and medications.

A Son of the Soil Giving Back
The Foundation is led by its President and Founder, Alabo (Hon.) Boma Iyaye, DSSRS, (Esq), a proud son of Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area and the Executive Director, Finance and Administration, of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC).
Through the Foundation, Alabo Iyaye has made the welfare of the elderly in his community a yearly commitment. The outreach is an example of public service that begins at home, bringing healthcare to the doorsteps of those who built the community and often find it hardest to reach a hospital.

An Invitation to the Elderly
The Foundation warmly invites all elderly residents aged 70 and above to attend. Families, neighbours and community leaders are urged to help the elderly get to the Civic Hall on both days.
Your health matters. Come, get checked and stay healthy.
Fifika Chiri Foundation: Serving humanity with compassion.
posts.summary: The Fifika Chiri Foundation, led by Alabo (Hon.) Boma Iyaye, EDFA, NDDC, will hold a free medical outreach for residents aged 70 and above at Bolo Civic Hall on 12th and 13th November 2026, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. daily.

The event was marked by prayers, thanksgiving, and fellowship as the family celebrated God’s goodness.

posts.body:
𝗢𝗚𝗨/𝗕𝗢𝗟𝗢 𝗖𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗖𝗜𝗟 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗜𝗥𝗠𝗔𝗡 𝗪𝗘𝗟𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘𝗦 𝗙𝗖𝗧 𝗠𝗜𝗡𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗥 𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗘𝗫𝗖𝗘𝗟𝗟𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗬, 𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗘𝗙 𝗕𝗔𝗥𝗥. 𝗘𝗭𝗘𝗡𝗪𝗢 𝗡𝗬𝗘𝗦𝗢𝗠 𝗪𝗜𝗞𝗘, 𝗖𝗢𝗡!
𝗧𝗢 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘𝗛𝗢𝗟𝗗𝗘𝗥𝗦' 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗧𝗢𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗥𝗢𝗪.


The Executive Chairman of Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area, Chief Vincent Nemiebokaa, Esq., has warmly welcomed the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, and National Leader of the Rainbow Coalition, His Excellency, Chief Barr. Ezenwo Nyesom Wike, CON, to the council area for a Stakeholders' Engagement scheduled to hold tomorrow, Friday, 13th November 2026.
The Chairman announced that the engagement will take place at the Alabo A.C. Iyaye Memorial Hall, Ogu, and described it as an important gathering that will bring the people of the area together with one of the most prominent political figures in Rivers State and Nigeria.

According to him, the programme will provide a valuable opportunity for political leaders, traditional rulers, community stakeholders, youths and other critical groups to interact, strengthen existing relationships and deliberate on issues of mutual interest. He added that the discussions will also focus on the continued development of the people of Ogu/Bolo.
Chief Nemiebokaa said the council area is delighted to host a leader whose political influence, experience and contributions to governance continue to shape political and developmental conversations across Rivers State and the country at large.
He noted that the visit reflects the importance of dialogue, unity and cooperation among leaders and stakeholders in driving progress at the grassroots. He expressed confidence that the engagement would deepen understanding among the various groups in the area and create a platform for shared ideas on the way forward.
The Chairman also called on residents, community leaders, traditional institutions and youths to turn out in large numbers and conduct themselves in an orderly manner, so that the event will be remembered as a successful and peaceful gathering.
"We look forward to a memorable and fruitful engagement as we unite in the spirit of progress, partnership and shared development," the Chairman said.
Chief Nemiebokaa once again extended a warm welcome to the Minister, saying: "Welcome to Ogu/Bolo, Your Excellency!"


Signed:
Chief Vincent Nemiebokaa, Esq.
Executive Chairman,
Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area.

posts.body:
The Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area, under the leadership of the Executive Chairman, Chief Vincent Nemieboka, Esq., on Wednesday, 18th November 2026, officially flagged off the 2026 ₦150,000 bursary scheme for indigent students of Ogu/Bolo origin in tertiary institutions.

The first phase of the programme witnessed the disbursement of ₦37.5 million in cash to 250 students, with each beneficiary receiving ₦150,000 to support their academic needs.

Addressing the beneficiaries, the Executive Chairman urged students to prioritise education, emphasising that no course of study is more important than another.
[Image 2]
 He noted that success depends largely on dedication, discipline, hard work and determination rather than one's chosen academic discipline.

He advised the beneficiaries to utilise the funds judiciously by  purchasing textbooks and addressing other essential academic expenses.

Speaking on the selection process, Chief Nemieboka maintained that the bursary scheme was free, fair and devoid of political considerations, favouritism or nepotism.

 He clarified that the programme was strictly intended for genuine indigenes of Ogu/Bolo Local Government Area who meet the established eligibility requirements, particularly those who used their Ogu/Bolo Local Government identification during admission.

In a significant assurance to the students, Chief Nemieboka promised that the bursary scheme would remain a continuous educational support programme throughout his tenure as Executive Chairman. 
He assured the students that as long as he remains in office, the initiative will continue to support eligible Ogu/Bolo students in their academic pursuits.
[Image 3]
He further announced that the second and third phases of the bursary scheme, including eligible postgraduate students, would commence as soon as possible.

In another major highlight of the ceremony, the Executive Chairman challenged students to strive for academic excellence, 𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐫𝐞𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐨𝐟 ₦𝟐 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐎𝐠𝐮/𝐁𝐨𝐥𝐨 𝐬𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐰𝐡𝐨 𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐮𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐚 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭-𝐂𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬 𝐝𝐞𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐱𝐭 𝐚𝐜𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐦𝐢𝐜 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫.

He encouraged the students to embrace hard work, discipline and academic commitment, assuring them that exceptional academic performance would receive recognition and support from his administration.

The Chairman reaffirmed his commitment to educational development and youth empowerment, urging the beneficiaries to remain focused and become responsible citizens who will contribute meaningfully to the growth and development of Ogu/Bolo.

𝗦𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗲𝗱:
Chesime Solomon Michael
Chief Press Secretary
Ogu/Bolo LGA.
